The city has two Major League Baseball (MLB) teams: the Chicago Cubs of the National League play in Wrigley Field on the North Side; and the Chicago White Sox of the American League play in Rate Field on the South Side
items.note: Answer should also accept just "Cubs and White Sox". Note the White Sox park is now Rate Field (formerly Guaranteed Rate Field / U.S. Cellular Field), in case that ever becomes a question.

items.quote: Wrigley Field is well-known for its ivy-covered brick outfield wall
the Chicago River is dyed green in observance of Saint Patrick's Day
Cloud Gate is a public sculpture by artist Anish Kapoor that is the centerpiece of Grainger Plaza at Millennium Park
there is a widely shared consensus among most Chicagoans and aficionados that ketchup is an unacceptable addition
winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls

The term Ferris wheel comes from the designer of the best known early example, George Washington Gale Ferris Jr., whose Ferris Wheel Company built a large amusement for the Chicago World's Columbian Exposition in 1893
items.note: Rechecked after rewording; 'star attraction' no longer claims a debut, so the pre-1893 wheels (Somers, Atlantic City 1891) no longer contradict it. One answer.

items.quote: The Willis Tower, formerly known and still commonly referred to as the Sears Tower
items.note: Naming rights came with a 2009 lease with the Willis Group (announced March 2009, name effective July 2009), so the "renamed in 2009" premise holds.
